title: Does the 'planning-ahead' circuit also plan deceptively? A decomposed interpretability test of forward-looking deception

original_idea.body:
# Does the 'planning-ahead' circuit also plan deceptively? A decomposed interpretability test of forward-looking deception

**Problem:** Anthropic found Claude 3.5 Haiku plans ahead (picks rhyme words early). Deception research worries about hidden multi-step plans. Sub-problem: in a small open model on a task where the honest and deceptive answers diverge, can we detect the deceptive target encoded BEFORE it's verbalized — i.e. does the model 'plan' the deception in advance?

**Direction:** Decompose 'detect hidden deceptive reasoning' into a forward-planning probe. Set up a simple scenario where a model is incentivized to give a misleading answer (e.g. a known open 'sandbagging on a test' or 'flattering wrong answer' setup). Probe early-position activations for the eventual misleading answer and measure how many tokens in advance the deceptive target is linearly decodable.

**Why it matters:** Connects a celebrated interpretability result (planning-ahead) to deception detection. Lead-time-of-deceptive-plan is a striking, communicable metric. Single GPU, open weights, no training — a model-organism-style probe scoped to 30h.

**Relevant context:** Anthropic Circuit Tracing 'plans ahead' result; deception_scheming open problem on encoded reasoning; logit-lens/probing in TransformerLens.
